data.body:
Review remediation record (2026-08-21) for this ticket's plan — moved out of the description to fit the plan-review admission cap. Five blocking gaps were found and closed; the constraints they produced now live in the description, and this comment preserves the investigation trail.

- The `32767` oracle was wrong. The original AC verified consolidation with `grep -rn "32767\|32000" src/rebar/_engine` "returns one file". That oracle could never pass: `32767` occurs in FOUR files and most occurrences must survive — `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py:41` `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` (Cloud's limit, in scope), `rebar_reconciler/runtime.py:46` `_DEFAULT_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` (the runtime default), `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:60,64` (the DC `jira.text.field.character.limit` default-value quoted from Atlassian docs), and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:244-257` (prose citing JRASERVER-28519 for why 32767 is only a DC default). Deleting those would delete sourced product knowledge. The construct being consolidated is the fit-for-send composition, not the number, so the AC was rewritten to an observable behavioural property: the dedup key is derived from the bytes actually sent.

- Only ONE of two mutation-enactment consumers was in Scope. The plan scoped `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:368-379` (create path) but missed `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:375-384` (update path), which is structurally identical — same `entry.get("body", "")` read, same single-attempt `client.add_comment(issue_key, body)`, same `_record_comment_id` follow-up. Leaving it out would have kept the update path sending the un-fitted `body` while the key came from `wire_body`: the exact drift this leaf closes, on half the traffic. Both are now in Scope and both take `entry["wire_body"]` with a pre-cutover fallback to `body` so an in-flight queue does not break.

- The `fit_comment` port and its two implementers were unscoped. `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:481` declares `fit_comment(self, body: str) -> str`, contract "return exactly the marker-free body the backend's SEND path lands"; implementers are `adapters/jira/backend.py:154` (Cloud) and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:303` (DC), both delegating to `outbound_comments.fit_comment_as_sent` (`outbound_comments.py:290`). Decision recorded: `fit_comment_as_sent` is RETAINED as a thin wrapper over `fit_for_send(...).landed_text`, so the Protocol signature and both implementers keep working unchanged and only callers that need the wire bytes move.

- "Adapters only encode and send" was under-specified. Made explicit: `acli_cli_ops.add_comment:531`, `adapters/jira/backend.add_comment` and DC's `sanitize_comment` stop fitting/encoding independently; `wire_body` is carried on the mutation entry so the bytes are computed once; the send path writes `wire_body` verbatim and, where an adapter genuinely must encode at send time, it must receive the SAME codec instance `fit_for_send` was given. A second codec instance, or a second read of the cutover flag, re-opens the drift, so an identity assertion pins it.

- A stale claim in Context, corrected. Context asserted that `codec.normalize_outbound(...)` at `outbound_comments.py:572` is "still an unmatched extra step". That call is no longer there: the region now derives BOTH keys through `_normalize_comment_body` under bug `17c3-2f6e-a5e0-438c` ("BOTH keys must be produced by ONE decoder"), which already closed that specific asymmetry. The remaining gap this leaf addresses is narrower and real — the key PREDICTS the wire the send path will produce, rather than being taken from the bytes actually sent.

- Housekeeping: the original description carried the whole remediation block and the Acceptance Criteria block twice, including the superseded `grep 32767` criterion. The duplicates were removed and the corrected criteria kept.
